result.topic_en: Notes on integrals of the form ∫x^k dx/(1−x^3)^{m/3}, using algebraic substitutions to reduce them to one another or to circular functions, together with series expansions and sketches of an S-shaped curve.

methods.what: Integral of x^2/(1-x^3)^{1/3} or ^{2/3} is algebraic
Substitution 1-x^3+x^3y^3=0 reduces ∫x dx/(1-x^3)^{2/3} to a rational integral, hence dependent on circular functions
The same substitution applied to ∫x dx/(1-x^3)^{1/3}
Series inversion giving x as a series in y, and the cube root (1-x^3)^{1/3} as a series in y
